text.p: Swedish power company Sydkraft AB said on Thursday its 1996 profits were largely unchanged despite a dry year which normally has a negative impact on profits.
Profit after financial items amounted to 2.504 billion crowns ($335.7 million) in 1996 and 2.499 billion crowns in 1995.
The 1996 profit was helped by smaller net financial costs which narrowed to 956 million crowns from 1.04 billion in 1995 following a strong cash flow and reduced interest rate costs.
"This was despite the acquisition of 20 percent of (Swedish power and forestry group) Graningeverken AB for about 1.8 billion crowns," the company said in a statement.
But operating profit was hurt by significantly decreased hydro-electric power production as 1996 was such a dry yea.
Operating profit after depreciation fell to 3.34 billion crowns from 3.49 billion crowns.
Sydkraft proposed to raise its dividend to four crowns a share for 1996 from 3.75 crowns a year earlier.
